Project plan and code: https://github.com/cafe2913/dokdo-gull (see README.md)
summary: Dokdo Gull is a public web tool that plays NASA SPHEREx images of one patch of sky in time order, so that anything that moved or changed brightness stands out. You enter an object name or a Right Ascension and declination; the tool finds every SPHEREx spectral image of that position, combines the images of each visit, and shows the visits as a time-lapse that you can play, blink between two dates, subtract, or stack. It marks where a catalogued object should be on each date and measures how far it actually moved, overlays Gaia stars, builds a spectrum from 0.75 to 5 micrometres on the fly, and shows the same field in 2MASS, WISE and DSS. On the challenge's test targets it measured Barnard's Star moving 9.9 arcseconds in 360 days (catalogue prediction: 10.3), Epsilon Indi B moving 6.6 (6.7) and WISE 0855 moving 3.5 (3.6), and it shows the variable stars RW Aurigae and R Draconis changing brightness. SPHEREx returns far more images than any one person can look through; a tool that needs only a web browser lets anyone help look for moving and changing objects.
details: Dokdo Gull plays NASA SPHEREx images of one sky position in time order, so anything that moved or changed brightness stands out. WHAT IT DOES: a time-lapse with one frame per SPHEREx visit on the same north-up grid and brightness scale; blink between two visits; subtract one visit from another; stack all visits; ticks at the position a catalogued object should have on each date, with the measured shift next to the predicted one; a Gaia DR3 overlay moved to each date; a spectrum from 0.75 to 5 micrometres built from the wavelength of every image, and a chart of brightness over time; contamination flags near the target and saturated pixels painted on the image; the same field in 2MASS, WISE and DSS; coordinates in the URL and an embed mode. The archive query names no data release, so new SPHEREx images are included automatically. HOW IT WORKS: a name is resolved with SIMBAD and moved along its proper motion; the IRSA TAP service lists the SPHEREx spectral images covering the position; cutouts are downloaded from IRSA; the zodiacal light model and background are subtracted; images are grouped into visits, aligned on a 3-arcsecond grid and combined with a median, one detector at a time; the target is measured in every image. Saturated stars are measured in a ring outside the core, which shows changes but not total brightness. WHAT WE CHECKED: Barnard's Star moved 9.9 arcsec in 360 days (catalogue: 10.3); Epsilon Indi B 6.6 in 522 days (6.7); WISE 0855 3.5 in 163 days (3.6), with no Gaia counterpart; RW Aurigae was about 1.45 times brighter in 2026 than in September 2025; R Draconis fell to about 0.3 times its June 2025 brightness. The five test targets are precomputed and play at once; other positions are computed on request and depend on the IRSA archive being reachable. TOOLS: Python (Astropy, reproject, NumPy, SciPy, FastAPI, Streamlit), JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Aladin Lite, GitHub Pages, Render. Code: https://github.com/cafe2913/dokdo-gull USE OF SI: the source code was generated with Claude (Anthropic) at the team's direction and is labelled in every file and commit; Claude also helped draft this text. No AI-generated images, video or audio are used.
dataRefs: SPHEREx spectral images, NASA/IPAC Infrared ScienceArchive (IRSA)
